correctness.rationale: KKT conditions yield exact active-cell Jacobians. All support/sign cells have strictly feasible samples. Piecewise-affine integration makes largest induced infinity matrix norm the global Lipschitz coefficient and realizes it with a finite distinct-input pair. Exchange argument implies sorted-prefix support; Cauchy–Schwarz plus a two-dimensional largest eigenvalue proves the dimension-sharp weight envelope and rigid full-support equality. Python standard-library verifier confirmed 464 finite rational/analytic examples, not used as proof of infinite cases.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Closest published published-finding corpus statement gives a general weighted cross-polytope constraint projection in l_p and a finite maximum of linear operator norms. The squared weighted l1 penalty proximal map differs: Jacobian denominator 1+alpha sum of squares instead of an active weight-square normalization, and its full-domain map is a resolvent, not constrained projection. Thus that broader family does not imply the finite alpha weight-envelope or dimension-four equality. A general inequality for rank-one contractions might cover part of Step 3, but not the all-active-support maximum and equality classification.

value.rationale: Exclusive-lasso proximal maps are used for structured sparsity. The exact coefficient computes worst-case coordinatewise sensitivity without enumerating all supports; its sharp normalized envelope exposes sqrt-dimension growth and unique anisotropic worst weights, whereas uniform weights have bounded amplification and maximize the envelope only in dimension four. This is a specific robustness classification absent from the source algorithms, not a claim that the proximal map or Jacobian are novel.
